header: Bioinorganic Chemistry. 7.1 O2 is in fact highly toxic to many organisms. Oxygen carriers bound to metalloproteins enable the transport and storage of $O_2$ in organisms.

subquestions.text_open: 7.1.1 Arthropods transport oxygen using hemocyanin. Hemocyanin is an oligomeric protein containing a pair of closely spaced Cu atoms. Colorless deoxyhemocyanin A [Cu(I)] is represented below. A binds one molecule of $\mathrm{O_2}$ to form bright-blue protein B. Given that Cu is in the +2 oxidation state in B, write the SMILES string of B (for example, A may be represented as '[N][Cu]([N])[N].[N][Cu]([N])[N]').

text_images.description: Simplified representation of the dicopper(I) center in deoxyhemocyanin A. The diagram is labeled with a bold uppercase A at the bottom center and is left-right symmetric. A central $Cu$ atom in the left half is connected by three straight lines to three $N$ atoms at the upper-left, directly left, and lower-left positions. These three $N$ atoms are joined in sequence by two arcs curving outward to the left: the upper-left $N$ is connected to the directly-left $N$, and the directly-left $N$ is connected to the lower-left $N$. A second central $Cu$ atom in the right half is similarly connected by three straight lines to three $N$ atoms at the upper-right, directly right, and lower-right positions. These three $N$ atoms are joined in sequence by two arcs curving outward to the right: the upper-right $N$ is connected to the directly-right $N$, and the directly-right $N$ is connected to the lower-right $N$. A long downward-curving arc at the bottom directly connects the lower-left $N$ and lower-right $N$ atoms.

subquestions.text_open: 7.1.2 Hemerythrin is a member of a special family of proteins containing a diiron center. In addition to coordination by amino-acid side chains and two bridging carboxylates, the two iron atoms are bridged by a common diatomic anion. Hemerythrin C is represented below (the diatomic bridging ligand is not shown), and C binds one molecule of $\mathrm{O_2}$ to form D. Given that $\mathrm{O_2}$ coordinates to only one Fe atom and that the diatomic bridging ligand provides some noncovalent stabilization to $\mathrm{O_2}$, write the SMILES string of D.

text_images.description: Simplified representation of the diiron center in hemerythrin C. C: '[R]/C1=O/[Fe]([*])([*])O/C([*])=O\[Fe]([*])([*])O1', where * denotes a site at which Fe coordinates to the imidazole group of His and may be omitted here.

subquestions.text_open: 7.1.3 CO is well known to strongly inhibit the binding of $\mathrm{O_2}$ to myoglobin, so suppressing CO coordination is essential. In fact, the structure of myoglobin weakens the binding of CO to the protein. Using the simplified myoglobin structure above, explain why CO binds less strongly to myoglobin than $\mathrm{O_2}$, considering the coordination geometries of CO and $\mathrm{O_2}$ and their noncovalent interactions. (No more than 100 words.)

text_images.description:
Simplified structure of the myoglobin coordination site, drawn with black lines on a white background.

A five-membered ring near the top bears the labels HN at the lower left and N at the upper right, with single- and double-bond lines in and around the ring. A downward-curving line from the lower-right side of the ring extends toward the upper-right region of an elliptical structure below.

An approximately elliptical ring of curved lines occupies the center. Four N labels appear around it at the upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, and lower-right positions, and Fe is labeled at the center.

A vertical line extends downward from Fe through the lower part of the ellipse to the label His below.

The Chinese caption at the bottom reads “Simplified myoglobin structure” in the English-localized version. SMILES: '[Fe][*].[N].[N].[N].[N].C1=CN=CN1', where * denotes the site at which Fe coordinates to the imidazole group of His and may be omitted here.
